state.goal: Find the smallest adequate toolchain for CanLang apps first deployed on Cloudflare's managed platform. Adoption leads; token-economical AI source and canonical SaaS primitives constrain the design. Reusing generic capabilities is required, as illustrated by the user's rejection of a new UTF-8 library. Only research/recommendations are requested now; building compiler, infrastructure, runtime or standard-library code is outside this round.
state.status: There are 44 CanLang sources, an existing Python grammar parser and 20 handwritten JavaScript output illustrations including CanCRM whose UI updates are being finished. Neither imported shared libraries, the semantic compiler nor operation services exist yet. The required application artifact is JavaScript ES modules emitted directly from .can for workerd. The possible standard-library implementation uses TypeScript at authoring time and produces checked JavaScript during its separate release process, without generating TypeScript apps. The compiler host language remains outside this selection; consistency of host languages alone does not warrant throwing away parser work.
state.platform: UTF-8 byte conversions and their streams already come from TextEncoder/TextDecoder in Workers. HTTP fetch/Request/Response, streams, Web Crypto, Intl and JS built-ins are also available. Managed D1/R2/DO/Queues/email still require Cloudflare provisioning/bindings; the open workerd engine does not furnish that control plane. Node compatibility offers an incomplete surface, and Wrangler-provided stubs may import yet fail when called. Under current documentation compatibility_date from 2026-08-04 onward activates Node compatibility by default, whereas older releases have distinct flag rules. Release/date pinning and checking the particular dependency APIs remain necessary. Primary material: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/web-standards/ ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/nodejs/ ; https://github.com/cloudflare/workerd
state.packaging: Wrangler's supplied path handles bundling via esbuild, conditional exports for workerd, development, uploads, dry-run review and generated Worker settings. A Wrangler version change may carry an esbuild change. Its --no-bundle route leaves code untouched and omits bundled polyfills. Keeping esbuild as a separately owned pinned build offers direct artifact/build-setting control, with module and polyfill compatibility work to reproduce where needed. Direct platform-API deployment affords upload-level control and can eliminate Wrangler as a dependency, but still needs module/asset construction, credential/configuration handling, resource creation/update behavior and integration for local execution/testing. Evidence contains no benchmark establishing a faster approach. Documentation basis: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/bundling/ ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/configuration/#generated-wrangler-configuration
state.examples: The language's BDD cases use independent expected values, invoke generated real operations, isolate rows, ensure rejection leaves committed effects unchanged and suppress actual provider calls. Cloudflare's present @cloudflare/vitest-plugin hosts Vitest in workerd with Miniflare and bindings, separating storage by file and offering helpers for queue delivery, scheduled events, DO alarms and migrations. That file boundary does not isolate table rows: emitted fixtures/reset logic must cover the row boundary. A dedicated workerd host can avoid Vitest conventions/dependencies and specialize CanLang execution; it would undertake process setup, binding configuration, isolated state, effect verification and results/recovery. Neither arrangement establishes live-service behavior, distributed safety or measured production throughput. The initial automated route should be singular rather than accompanied by redundant runners and simulations. References used: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/testing/vitest-integration/ ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/testing/vitest-integration/isolation-and-concurrency/ ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/testing/vitest-integration/test-apis/
state.boundaries: Language-specific implementation comprises selected-source/import closure, typed/effect-checked definitions, generated CRUD schemas and defaults, permissions preceding queries, dependency-triggered final invariants, pre-state locks, bounded evaluation, precise numeric/storage/wire conversion, operation replay identity, atomic effects, interface/frontend production and explicit schema-transition semantics. Existing auth/ICU/MCP/decimal implementations may fit portions after contract review, not automatically satisfy this collection of rules. Worker configuration, SQL changes, assets, tests and version-pinned library release dependency information may be generated internally. App source must not be burdened with wrapper declarations, repeated source/package lists or a second authored build format. Real resource IDs, secrets and service mappings require deployment context and cannot be guessed from app identity.

packaging.instructions: Identify the most suitable first release packaging/deployment path from these alternatives. Consider control over artifacts as well as existing integration and maintenance burden, with no assumed benchmark or correctness advantage attached to a name.

criteria.wrangler_bundle: Emit CanLang's JS, derived configuration and companion outputs and use version-pinned Wrangler's standard bundle/deploy route. Reuse its managed-platform and development handling while retaining dependence on its esbuild choices and release behavior.
criteria.explicit_esbuild: Run an explicitly pinned esbuild packager owned by CanLang before Wrangler --no-bundle uploads the result. Take tighter control of build artifacts/settings and also own module discovery and needed polyfills no longer provided by normal bundling.
criteria.api_upload: Make Cloudflare API uploads the principal deployment mechanism in place of Wrangler. Control platform requests and avoid that tool dependency, but provide matching artifact packaging, credentials/settings, resource updates and local dev/test integration.
criteria.unresolved: Keep this tool selection provisional until another deployment constraint or demonstrable capability gap gives enough reason to select a particular path.

examples.instructions: Determine the initial canonical automated route for the existing example notation. Balance reusable workerd testing with specialized direct control, ensuring row-level isolation and actual operation invocation remain obligations rather than presumed successes.

criteria.official_vitest: Emit Vitest cases for @cloudflare/vitest-plugin together with CanLang fixtures and assertions on effects. Rely on maintained workerd/binding support, accepting that dependency and adding row isolation to the documented file isolation.
criteria.custom_workerd: Execute generated cases with an exclusive CanLang runner controlling workerd. Obtain specialized orchestration/reporting without Vitest conventions while implementing binding/process lifecycle, independent row state, effect checks and recovery.
criteria.unresolved: Do not select a host yet because the described tools and language example contract leave the adequacy of either initial route unsettled.
